scientific_question: When an exact frozen graph candidate makes one source hypothesis uniquely compatible, does the POSITIVE observation identify that source if graph identity itself remains unknown?

source.prior_source_cases: Glanville annual sources are current-state; Algar & Hungarian original wetland sources do not establish ancestry. No new field outcome is opened.

fixed_inputs.graph_universe: same all 64 directed simple three-node one-step operators on A/B/C, without response-dependent graph selection
fixed_inputs.inverse_logic: Project compatible (rule,hypothesis) pairs to source-hypothesis IDs; do not condition on unknown rule after looking at the answer.
fixed_inputs.scope: complete ONLY for fixed synthetic 64 graph × 3 declared source hypothesis panel, not historical sources or natural movement

expected.independent_count_proof: With 3 disjoint two-edge groups (outgoing edges of A,B,C), each singleton source requires its own two edges. Number of graphs supporting exactly k sources = C(3,k)*3^(3-k). For k=0..3: 27,27,9,1. Joint compatible assignments = 27 + 2*9 + 3=48.

exemplar_source_unique_given_rule.hypothetical_rule: hub A↔C↔B with no A↔B, one step

expected.status_semantics: globally one hypothesis only if the projection onto source IDs over the entire declared set of compatible rule-source pairs is singleton; zero compatible pairs is a universe falsification status, not identification
